title: Rig wiring
_readme: THE OPERATOR'S OWN WIRING, at <data_dir>/hardware/rig.json. It REPLACES the
merging with it -- a merge would mean a channel you deleted came back, and
there would be no way to say 'this box has no vacuum line'.
TWO SECTIONS, ON PURPOSE. `channels` is what a channel MEANS; `pins` is where
it IS. That split is what lets a box generation be swapped without touching
meaning, and it is what TG226 checks. Collapsing them into one map would make
that rule unwritable. Writing them together in one document is what makes the
THIS SCHEMA CHECKS SHAPE, NOT SENSE. Whether a pin is one this board has,
whether two channels share one, and whether every response port has its own
strobe slot are TG227, TG228 and TG229 -- and they run against the COMPOSED
ChannelMap, so a problem is reported once regardless of which half caused it.
A PIN CHANGE IS NOT A TASK CHANGE. Specs name channels, never numbers (D15),
so editing this file changes the bytes every task compiles to and moves no
spec_hash. That is the design working, and it is also why the listing header
carries a pinout hash: without it the review artifact is blind to a remap.

rig_version.description: The shape of THIS file. Bumped when a section moves or changes meaning, never when a rig is rewired.

derived_from.description: The shipped pinout this rig started as. Recorded so 'a Mega, wired how?' has an answer the operator did not have to remember.

edited_at.description: Stamped by the store on write. Present in a stored document, absent in one being submitted.

pin_range.description: The board's own pin numbering, so TG227 can say 'a Mega has 0-53' rather than quoting the compiler's binding-encoding constant.

channels.description: What each channel means. Keys are channel names and are referenced by every task spec, so renaming one is a rename in every task that names it.

kind.description: Resolution is BY KIND for the structural channels (D15): the template asks for 'the engagement channel', not for a name. Exactly one engagement channel, one cue and one vacuum must resolve, which is TG225.

label.description: What the operator calls it. Display only — never referenced by a spec, so renaming a label is free and renaming a channel is not.

well.description: Reward lines only: which response port this line serves. TG224 uses it to refuse a spec that rewards one well through the other's line — a mistake that looks correct in the listing and delivers water to the wrong side of the box.

port_slot.description: Response ports only: which family of per-port strobes this port reports with (strobe_vocab `port_slots`). Slots 1 and 2 are the historical _L/_R codes. Two ports on one slot are indistinguishable in the data, which is TG229.

pins.description: Where each channel is. Every key here must appear in `channels` and vice versa — TG226 reports both directions.

index.description: The board pin. Capped at 239 because lower.py encodes runtime-bound channels from 0xF0 up in the same byte — a pin there is not refused by the board, it is read as a per-trial binding. Whether it is a pin THIS board has is TG227.

watch_bit.description: Watchable inputs only: this channel's bit position in TgNode.watchMask. Must be dense and 0-based over exactly the watchable channels (TG226) — a gap addresses the wrong channel rather than none. Eight bits is the hard ceiling, TG_MAX_WATCH.

channel_name.description: Lower snake case. The same shape a spec's identifiers take, because a channel name is written into specs by hand.
